commands.author: pdurlej

target.title: fix(signal): expose mention facts in inbound context
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal group mention gating now has native mention metadata available, but the delivered-turn decision facts are only visible inside the Signal monitor. Downstream prompt/tool context cannot inspect whether the inbound group message had native mention metadata, whether `requireMention` was enforced for that delivered turn, or which mention path matched the bot. That makes native-only group behavior hard to debug and forces consumers to infer channel-specific facts from text.

## Summary

- Exposes Signal mention-gating facts on the generic inbound message context.
- Adds `CanDetectMention`, `HasAnyMention`, `EffectiveWasMentioned`, `MentionShouldSkip`, and `MentionSource` for delivered native/text mention decisions, while reusing the existing canonical `GroupRequireMention` field.
- Keeps the Signal mention source literal typed so SDK/context consumers can rely on `"native"` vs `"mention_pattern"`.

## Stack

This is stacked after #96738 (`fix(signal): detect native bot mentions in group gating`). Until #96738 lands, this PR's diff will include that dependency.

## Production impact

No new outbound behavior. This only makes already-computed delivered-turn mention gating facts inspectable by prompts, tests, and plugin/channel contracts. Skipped Signal turns still return before prompt/tool context is built, so this PR intentionally does not expose a public skipped-turn context field.

## Evidence

- Focused Signal/channel tests cover native mention facts being projected into inbound context:
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/channels/inbound-event/context.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts`
- Plugin SDK runtime mock tests cover `Mention*` parity with production inbound context.
- Broader affected-context regression suite passed:
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/openclaw-tools.plugin-context.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-utils.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.test.ts extensions/memory-core/index.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/tools.citations.test.ts src/channels/inbound-event/context.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts`
- Focused SDK mock test passed:
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-sdk/test-helpers/plugin-runtime-mock.test.ts`
- Plugin SDK API check passed:
  `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check`
- Production TypeScript check passed:
  `pnpm tsgo:prod`

### Redacted Runtime Proof

The current-head terminal proof is in the Evidence update below. Earlier local proof from an older head was removed from this body to avoid stale field names and stale commit evidence.

### Operational Signal group evidence (2026-06-26)

A private Signal group smoke was run after a production config hotfix that kept the group-bound agent responding without changing Docker permissions. The private runtime intentionally stayed on its deployed OpenClaw release instead of being advanced to this PR stack today; the facts below are operational evidence for the real Signal group route, not an additional claim that this PR head is live-deployed.

Sanitized facts:

- `openclaw config validate` against `/run/user/1000/openclaw/openclaw.json`: `valid=true`, exit `0`.
- `openclaw-gateway.service`: `active/running`, `NRestarts=0`.
- A native Signal mention from a group participant produced an outbound group reply; the journal recorded `delivered reply to group` at `2026-06-26T13:03:19+02:00`.
- Latest group-bound Signal session metadata for the private family agent: `systemSent=true`, `abortedLastRun=false`.
- Journal after the smoke: `Failed to inspect sandbox image` count `0`.

Deployment note: the private runtime is not being upgraded to this stack today because that would mix the PR validation with an unrelated Docker sandbox repair. The long-term Docker/rootless sandbox fix is being tracked separately.

## Tests

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-sdk/test-helpers/plugin-runtime-mock.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/channels/inbound-event/context.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/openclaw-tools.plugin-context.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-utils.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.test.ts extensions/memory-core/index.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/tools.citations.test.ts src/channels/inbound-event/context.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts`
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check`
- `pnpm tsgo:prod`

### Evidence update

Current-head proof on `codex/signal-mention-facts-context` (`4bcda17af9`):

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/channels/inbound-event/context.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/test-helpers/plugin-runtime-mock.test.ts
[test] passed 3 Vitest shards in 15.32s

$ node --max-old-space-size=8192 --import tsx scripts/generate-plugin-sdk-api-baseline.ts --check
OK docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256

$ git diff --check
# passed with no output
```

Current-head terminal proof at the real Signal event-handler boundary. The temporary harness imported production `createSignalEventHandler`, used the production native mention resolver and mention decision helper, and captured the `dispatchInboundMessage` boundary through the channel contract testing helper. The harness used only synthetic/redacted identifiers and was not committed.

```text
$ OC_PROOF_HEAD=4bcda17af9 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/monitor/signal-mention-context-proof.test.ts --silent=false --reporter=verbose
runtime-proof:environment
{
  "pr": 96862,
  "head": "4bcda17af9",
  "boundary": [
    "dispatchInboundMessage",
    "runtime-drop/pending-history"
  ],
  "privacy": "all ids, phone numbers, participant names, group ids, and message bodies are synthetic"
}

runtime-proof:#96862 native bot mention dispatchInboundMessage context
{
  "Body": "<redacted-rendered-bot-mention-message>",
  "CanDetectMention": true,
  "WasMentioned": true,
  "HasAnyMention": true,
  "GroupRequireMention": true,
  "EffectiveWasMentioned": true,
  "MentionShouldSkip": false,
  "MentionSource": "native"
}

runtime-proof:#96862 non-bot native mention runtime drop boundary
{
  "dispatchInboundMessageCalled": false,
  "skipBoundaryObserved": true,
  "pendingHistoryCount": 1,
  "pendingHistoryBody": "<redacted-rendered-non-bot-mention-message>",
  "nativeFacts": {
    "canDetectMention": true,
    "hasAnyMention": true,
    "mentionsBot": false
  },
  "mentionDecision": {
    "effectiveWasMentioned": false,
    "mentionShouldSkip": true
  }
}

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  1 passed (1)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 8.65s
```

Inspectable assertions covered:

- Native Signal bot mention reaches the delivered `dispatchInboundMessage` context with:
  `CanDetectMention=true`, `WasMentioned=true`, `HasAnyMention=true`,
  `GroupRequireMention=true`, `EffectiveWasMentioned=true`,
  `MentionShouldSkip=false`, `MentionSource="native"`.
- Native Signal mention of another participant does not dispatch; it is skipped into pending group history with the same production mention decision reporting `mentionShouldSkip=true`.
- `MsgContext.WasMentioned` remains the effective mention-gating result for delivered Signal turns.
- Existing `GroupRequireMention` remains the canonical require-mention policy field; the transient
  `RequireMention` alias was removed after review.
- `createPluginRuntimeMock` mirrors both `GroupRequireMention` and `MentionShouldSkip`.

No private Signal identifiers, phone numbers, participant names, group ids, or message bodies are used in this proof.
